whatItDoes: Continues Kentfield Fire Protection District’s special tax for paramedic services for four years, from July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2031. It starts at $107.50 per residential unit or per 1,000 square feet of developed nonresidential property, with annual increases of up to $4 beginning in 2028.
yesMeans: Approve this four-year tax continuation and its annual adjustment authority, with proceeds restricted to local paramedic services.
noMeans: Do not continue this levy; the current paramedic tax expires June 30, 2027.

parts.label: Rate and estimate
parts.what: The starting annual charge is $107.50 per residential unit or per 1,000 square feet of developed nonresidential property. Increases of up to $4 a year begin July 1, 2028. The District estimates $326,000 a year; that amount is an estimate.

parts.label: Restricted services and oversight
parts.what: Money must go into a separate special account and may fund only the stated paramedic-service purposes, including emergency response and keeping on-duty paramedics available through the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority. The ballot requires annual audits and public spending disclosure.

parts.label: Four-year limit and approval
parts.what: The continuation begins July 1, 2027 and expires June 30, 2031. At least two-thirds of votes cast on the measure must be yes. This tax applies only within this fire protection district, not throughout the whole paramedic authority.

whatItDoes: Continues County Service Area 27’s paramedic tax for four years, from July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2031, with a $107.50 starting charge and increases of up to $4 a year beginning in 2028. The ballot and full text describe the charge’s basis differently, as explained below.
yesMeans: Approve this four-year restricted paramedic-tax continuation, its annual adjustments, separate fund and collection rules.
noMeans: Do not continue this levy; the existing paramedic tax expires June 30, 2027.

parts.label: Different wording about the tax basis
parts.what: The ballot question and County Counsel analysis say $107.50 per residential unit or per 1,000 square feet of developed nonresidential property. The full measure’s rate clause instead says $107.50 per separately property-tax-billed parcel. This explainer preserves that difference rather than treating those charges as identical.

parts.label: Start and annual adjustments
parts.what: The continuation runs from July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2031. Annual increases of up to $4 begin July 1, 2028. The full text estimates $84,000 in the first year and says yearly collections can change with the number of taxable parcels and the annual adjustment.

parts.label: Restricted local services and oversight
parts.what: Money must go into a separate special fund and be used only for paramedic and emergency medical services through the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority. The ballot requires annual audits and public spending disclosure.

parts.label: Property definitions and exemptions
parts.what: The full text defines a residential unit as a building or portion with a separate bathroom and one kitchen. Hotels and motels count as nonresidential uses; floor area includes all enclosed floors measured to the outer walls. Property otherwise exempt from regular property tax, or on which none is levied that year, is exempt.

parts.label: Collection and spending limit
parts.what: County collection follows property-tax timing, penalties and unpaid-interest rules, with final exemption or relief decisions by the County Tax Collector. The constitutional spending limit is adjusted for the tax proceeds. The levy is not a tax based on property value or a property-sale tax.

parts.label: Approval and severability
parts.what: At least two-thirds of votes cast on Measure Y must be yes. If a court invalidates part of the measure or tax formula, the remaining provisions continue as far as the law allows.

whatItDoes: Continues the Paradise Cay dredging tax in County Service Area 29 for ten years, from July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2037. The charge starts at $2,200 per lot each year and rises automatically by 3% annually starting July 1, 2028.
yesMeans: Approve this ten-year tax continuation and automatic annual increases for the stated dredging work.
noMeans: Do not continue the levy; the existing dredging tax expires June 30, 2027.

parts.label: Rate and estimated revenue
parts.what: The starting annual charge is $2,200 per lot. It increases automatically by 3% each year beginning July 1, 2028. The County estimates about $272,800 a year.

parts.label: Dredging purposes
parts.what: Revenue may fund the purposes and projects stated in Measure Z: ongoing maintenance dredging in Paradise Cay’s principal waterways and the north and south entry channels to San Francisco Bay. It applies only within County Service Area29.

parts.label: Ten-year term and approval
parts.what: The extension begins July 1, 2027 and expires June 30, 2037. At least two-thirds of votes cast on Measure Z must be yes.

whatItDoes: Continues Inverness Public Utility District’s higher constitutional spending limit for fiscal years 2026–27 through 2029–30, using the combined total of all applicable revenue sources. It does not create a new assessment or increase a property-tax rate.
yesMeans: Allow the District to keep spending tax revenue above its base limit for another four years, through 2029–30.
noMeans: Do not approve the four-year adjustment. County Counsel says the District’s spending limit would fall, reducing funds available for its current service levels.

parts.label: What the spending limit does
parts.what: California’s constitutional appropriations limit caps how much tax revenue the District may spend. Voters may adjust that limit for up to four years at a time. This measure includes the combined total of applicable revenue sources for 2026–27 through 2029–30.

parts.label: No new tax authorization
parts.what: The measure changes spending authority. It does not authorize a new assessment or increase any property-tax rate.

parts.label: Approval threshold
parts.what: A simple majority of votes cast on Measure AA must be yes.

whatItDoes: Sets Stinson Beach County Water District’s constitutional spending limit at $1,536,312 for fiscal year 2026–27 and uses that base to determine the limits through 2029–30. It does not authorize a new assessment or increase a property-tax rate.
yesMeans: Approve the $1,536,312 base and the four-year spending-limit adjustment through fiscal year 2029–30.
noMeans: Do not approve this adjustment. County Counsel says the District’s spending limit would fall, reducing funds available for its current service levels.

parts.label: Base year and following years
parts.what: The proposed limit is $1,536,312 for 2026–27. That base is used to determine limits for 2026–27 through 2029–30; the measure does not say every later year has the same dollar limit.

parts.label: Spending authority, without a new tax
parts.what: The constitutional limit restricts spending of tax revenue. County Counsel says this measure continues authority to spend above the base limit and does not authorize a new assessment or increase any property-tax rate.

parts.label: Four-year adjustment and approval
parts.what: Voters may adjust the constitutional spending limit for up to four years at a time. A simple majority of votes cast on Measure EE must be yes.
